examples.en: The meeting opens at ten in the morning.
As soon as the National Assembly opened, a big debate began.
The chair declared the session open, and the meeting began.
Please arrive by 9 so you aren't late for the opening.

examples.ko: 연설자가 개회식에 늦게 도착해서 순서가 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: The speaker arrived late to the opening ceremony, so the order changed.

examples.ko: 총회가 예정보다 십 분 늦게 개회했어요.
examples.en: The general meeting opened ten minutes later than planned.

explain: 반대말은 '폐회하다'예요. 회의나 행사가 시작될 때만 쓰는 격식 있는 말이라 '수업을 시작하다'처럼 일상적인 일에는 어울리지 않아요. '개회식', '개회사', '개회 선언'처럼 묶어서 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The opening ceremony is held in the auditorium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의나 행사를 시작하는 공식 순서를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The formal ceremony that starts a meeting or event.

phrases.en: The chairperson declared the session open.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의를 시작한다고 공식적으로 말할 때 쓰는 격식 있는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression for officially starting a meeting.

phrases.en: The representative gave the opening speech.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 시작하며 하는 인사말을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the speech given at the start of an event.

explain_en: Its opposite is '폐회하다'. It is a formal word used only when a meeting or event begins, so it doesn't fit everyday things like starting a class. It often appears in compounds such as '개회식', '개회사' and '개회 선언'.

dis.h: formally open a meeting or session

p.n: The passive needs a subject marked with 가/이, so the same object sentence does not work.

examples.en: An accident happened, so an emergency meeting was held.
The team leader suddenly called an emergency meeting.
I couldn't eat lunch because of the emergency meeting.
I was late for my appointment because I attended an emergency meeting.
The emergency meeting ended in an hour.
Today's schedule all changed because of the emergency meeting.

explain: 갑자기 생긴 급한 일 때문에 여는 회의예요. '긴급회의를 열다', '긴급회의를 소집하다'처럼 쓰고, 회사와 뉴스에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 회사는 내일 아침 긴급회의를 열기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The company decided to hold an emergency meeting tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의를 시작하거나 하기로 정할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for holding a meeting.

phrases.en: All the team leaders attended the emergency meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의에 가서 함께한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to go and take part in the meeting.

phrases.example: 지금 긴급회의 중이라 전화를 못 받아요.
phrases.en: I'm in an emergency meeting now, so I can't answer the phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 회의가 진행되는 중이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the meeting is going on right now.

explain_en: It is a meeting held because of a sudden urgent matter. It is used as '긴급회의를 열다' or '긴급회의를 소집하다' and appears often at work and in the news.

examples.en: The union members held a rally in front of the company.
I joined the union as a member last year.
Most of the union members voted in favor of the strike.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 새 노조원을 환영하는 모임이 있어요.
examples.en: This weekend there is a gathering to welcome new union members.

examples.ko: 노조원에게는 여러 가지 복지 혜택이 있어요.
examples.en: Union members get various welfare benefits.
My friend, who is a union member, went to vote.

explain: '노동조합'을 줄인 '노조'에 사람을 뜻하는 '원'이 붙은 말이에요. 같은 사람을 '조합원'이라고도 해요. 회사 직원 전체가 아니라 노조에 가입한 사람만 가리키니까 '직원'과 구분해서 써요.

phrases.en: I am a union member at this company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '노조원'을 문장 끝에 넣어 자신이나 다른 사람의 신분을 말할 때 쓰는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite sentence ending that states someone's status as a union member.

phrases.en: The union members gathered and had a meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 노조에 가입한 여러 사람을 함께 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '들' refers to several union members as a group.

phrases.example: 우리 회사 조합원은 백 명이 넘어요.
phrases.en: Our company has more than a hundred union members.
phrases.nuance_ko: '노조원'과 같은 사람을 가리키는 비슷한 말이에요. '조합원'은 노조 외의 다른 조합 회원에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A synonym for the same person; '조합원' can also refer to members of other kinds of associations.

explain_en: It is '노조' (short for 노동조합, labor union) plus '원' (member). The same person is also called a '조합원'. It refers only to those who joined the union, not to all employees, so keep it separate from '직원'.

examples.en: A new plan is being discussed at the meeting.
That issue was discussed for a long time yesterday.
The budget will be discussed next week.

examples.ko: 논의되는 내용은 모두 메일로 알려 줄게요.
examples.en: I will send you everything that is discussed by email.
We decided after the opinions were fully discussed.
Several methods were discussed, so it is hard to choose.

explain: 안건이나 문제가 주어이고, 회의나 공식적인 자리에서 이야기가 오갈 때 써요. 친구끼리 편하게 이야기하는 일에는 잘 쓰지 않고, 그때는 '이야기하다'를 써요. 사람이 하면 '논의하다'예요.

phrases.example: 그 문제는 지금 회의에서 논의되고 있어요.
phrases.en: That issue is being discussed in the meeting now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 이야기가 오가는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the discussion is going on right now.

phrases.en: That topic hasn't been discussed yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 다루지 않았다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning it hasn't been covered yet.

phrases.en: It will be discussed again at the next meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로의 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a future plan.

explain_en: The subject is an agenda item or issue that is being talked over in a meeting or formal setting. For casual chats between friends use '이야기하다' instead. When a person does it, it is '논의하다'.

p.n: 토론되다 suggests debate with differing views.

examples.en: We discussed next week's schedule.
They are discussing the budget issue in the meeting.

examples.ko: 이 일은 가족과 먼저 논의해 보세요.
examples.en: Talk this over with your family first.
There is too much to discuss.
After a long discussion, we made a decision.

examples.ko: 두 팀이 따로 만나서 논의하면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I'd like the two teams to meet separately and discuss it.

explain: '이야기하다'보다 격식 있고, 결정을 내리려고 의견을 나눈다는 느낌이 있어요. '~을/를 논의하다', '~와/과 논의하다'로 써요. 친구와 수다를 떨 때는 쓰지 않고, 회의·직장·학교 발표에 어울려요.

phrases.en: Let's discuss this problem together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'는 한번 해 본다는 뜻이에요. 회의에서 제안할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-a/eo boda' means to give something a try. Use it to suggest something in a meeting.

phrases.en: This matter needs more discussion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 결정하기 전이라 이야기가 더 필요하다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a decision is not made yet and more talk is needed.

phrases.en: I discussed moving with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: '논의하다'보다 덜 딱딱해요. 가족이나 친구와 일상적인 일을 이야기할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is less stiff than '논의하다'. You can use it with family or friends about everyday matters.

explain_en: It is more formal than '이야기하다' and suggests exchanging opinions in order to reach a decision. Use '~을/를 논의하다' or '~와/과 논의하다'. It is not for chatting with friends; it fits meetings, work, and school presentations.

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 단과대가 열 개 있어요.
examples.en: Our university has ten colleges.

examples.ko: 공대는 이공 계열 단과대 중에서 가장 커요.
examples.en: The engineering college is the biggest of the science and engineering colleges.
Each college has its own student council.

examples.ko: 단과대 건물이 멀어서 수업 사이에 뛰어다녀요.
examples.en: The college buildings are far apart, so I run around between classes.

examples.ko: 경영대는 우리 학교에서 인기 있는 단과대예요.
examples.en: The business college is a popular college at our school.
Each college holds its own welcome party for new students.

explain: 한 대학교 안에 있는 큰 단위로, 공과대학, 인문대학, 경영대학 같은 것이에요. 보통 '공대', '인문대'처럼 줄여서 말해요. 단과대 아래에 여러 학과가 있어요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling goes to the engineering college.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공과대학'을 줄여서 말하는 단과대 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short name for the engineering college, one kind of 단과대.

phrases.en: The college's students are preparing the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 단과대에 속한 학생들을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for students belonging to a single college.

phrases.example: 우리 단과대 건물은 정문 옆에 있어요.
phrases.en: Our college building is next to the main gate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단과대가 쓰는 건물을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the building that a college uses.

explain_en: It is a large unit within one university, such as the college of engineering, humanities or business. People usually shorten the names, like '공대' and '인문대'. Several departments sit under each college.

examples.en: The interview requires the presence of someone from HR.
If you'd like to sit in, please tell us in advance.

examples.ko: 상담할 때 보호자 동석은 선택 사항이에요.
examples.en: A guardian being present during counseling is optional.

examples.ko: 동석 여부를 알려 주시면 자리를 준비할게요.
examples.en: If you let me know whether you'll join us, I'll prepare a seat.
I got a request to join them, so I stopped by briefly to say hello.

examples.ko: 회의에 동석 가능한 인원은 두 명뿐이에요.
examples.en: Only two people can sit in on the meeting.

explain: 모임, 식사, 상담, 회의처럼 같은 자리에 함께 있는 것을 말해요. '동석 여부', '동석 가능'처럼 안내문이나 공지에 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '같이 앉다', '자리를 함께하다'라고 풀어서 말해요.

phrases.example: 보호자 동석 가능이라고 안내문에 적혀 있어요.
phrases.en: The notice says a guardian may sit in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 함께 있어도 된다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used on notices to mean someone may be present too.

phrases.en: Please let us know in advance whether you will attend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같이 참석하는지 아닌지를 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask whether someone will be present or not.

phrases.en: There are three people sitting in altogether.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 자리에 함께 있던 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who was present at the gathering.

explain_en: It means being at the same gathering, meal, consultation or meeting together. It often appears in notices as '동석 여부' or '동석 가능'. In daily talk people spell it out as '같이 앉다' or '자리를 함께하다'.

en: to comment; to remark; to state

examples.en: At the meeting, people speak one by one in turn.
He raised his hand and spoke carefully.
May I speak too?
The CEO will speak in person today.

examples.ko: 누군가 발언할 때는 조용히 해 주세요.
examples.en: Please be quiet when someone is speaking.

examples.ko: 먼저 발언한 의견이 토론의 방향을 정했어요.
examples.en: The opinion stated first set the direction of the discussion.

explain: '말하다'와 달리 회의·토론·기자회견처럼 공식적인 자리에서 의견을 밝힐 때 써요. 친구와 수다를 떨 때는 쓰지 않아요. 명사 '발언'과 같이 '발언을 하다', '발언이 길다'로도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: He made a short statement at the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '발언'과 함께 쓰는 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural expression using the noun 발언.

phrases.en: He did not speak until the very end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적인 자리에서 의견을 말하지 않았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone did not voice an opinion in a formal setting.

phrases.en: I gave my opinion at the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 부드러운 말로, 일상에서도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, softer phrase that is common in daily speech too.

explain_en: Unlike plain 말하다, it is for stating an opinion in formal settings such as meetings, debates and press conferences. You would not use it for chatting with friends. The noun 발언 is also common: '발언을 하다', '발언이 길다'.

examples.ko: 잠시 쉬었다가 속개한 회의에서는 예산안부터 다루었어요.
examples.en: At the meeting resumed after a short break, they dealt with the budget first.
We resume the meeting after lunch.

examples.ko: 비가 그치면 경기를 속개할 거라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the game will resume once the rain stops.

examples.ko: 정전 때문에 멈췄던 수업을 한 시간 뒤에 속개했어요.
examples.en: The class stopped by the power outage resumed an hour later.

examples.ko: 재판장은 내일 오전 열 시에 재판을 속개한다고 했어요.
examples.en: The presiding judge said the trial will resume at ten tomorrow morning.

examples.ko: 협상을 속개하기로 해서 양측이 다시 만났어요.
examples.en: They decided to resume the negotiations, so both sides met again.

explain: 회의, 재판, 경기처럼 중간에 멈춘 공식적인 일을 다시 이어 갈 때 써요. 일상에서는 '다시 시작하다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: The meeting resumed after the break.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멈췄던 공식적인 일이 다시 이어졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a formal event that had stopped was picked up again.

phrases.en: The court will resume the trial tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재판이나 회의처럼 중간에 쉰 공식 일정을 다시 이어 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for continuing a formal proceeding such as a trial or meeting after a pause.

phrases.en: We restart the meeting after lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: '속개하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 일상에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'sokgaehada' but more natural in daily speech.

explain_en: It is used when an official event that stopped partway, such as a meeting, trial or match, picks up again. In everyday talk people often say '다시 시작하다' instead.

examples.en: The protesters linked arms and formed a scrum line.

examples.ko: 럭비 선수들이 경기 시작 전에 스크럼을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The rugby players formed a scrum before the match started.
We decided to run the new project with Scrum.
The union members broke their linked line and slowly dispersed.

examples.ko: 팬들이 스크럼처럼 어깨동무를 하고 응원가를 불렀어요.
examples.en: The fans put their arms over each other's shoulders like a scrum and sang the cheer song.

examples.ko: 개발팀은 매일 아침 스크럼 회의를 해요.
examples.en: The development team has a scrum meeting every morning.

explain: 럭비에서 선수들이 어깨를 맞대고 겨루는 대형이에요. 뉴스에서는 시위대가 팔을 끼고 줄을 이루는 모습에, 회사에서는 짧은 회의로 일하는 방식에 써요. '스크럼을 짜다'라는 짝말을 알아 두세요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀은 아침마다 스크럼 회의를 해요.
phrases.en: Our team holds a scrum meeting every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에서 짧게 진행 상황을 나누는 회의를 말할 때 '회의'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 회의 refers to the short work meetings used in companies.

phrases.en: The protesters locked arms and blocked the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 팔을 끼고 줄을 이룰 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for people linking arms to form a line.

phrases.example: 경기가 끝나자 선수들이 스크럼을 풀고 인사했어요.
phrases.en: When the game ended, the players broke the scrum and greeted each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짜 놓은 스크럼을 끝낼 때 '풀다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 풀다 when a formed scrum is broken up.

explain_en: In rugby it is the formation where players bind together and push. In the news it describes protesters linking arms in a line, and at work it names a method of working with short meetings. Remember the collocation '스크럼을 짜다' (to form a scrum).

en: to be mentioned; to be stated; to be talked about

examples.en: That name is often mentioned in the news.
The problem was not mentioned in the meeting.
Please check the mentioned contents again.
This book has been mentioned in many places.
It is scheduled to be mentioned next time.
The singer's name is being mentioned.

explain: '말하다'보다 딱딱하고, 어떤 일을 잠깐 꺼내서 이야기할 때 써요. '언급하다'는 말하는 사람이 주인공이고 '언급되다'는 말해진 내용이 주인공이에요. 뉴스와 글에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That book is often mentioned in interviews.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 번 이야기에 나올 때 '자주'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 자주 when something comes up many times.

phrases.en: That is mentioned in the manual.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글에 이미 적혀 있다는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something already stated in writing.

phrases.example: 그 사람 이름이 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.en: That person's name comes up often in the conversation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '언급되다'를 쉬운 말로 바꾼 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say 언급되다.

explain_en: Stiffer than the plain verb for saying, it is for bringing something up briefly. The active form has the speaker as subject; this passive has the thing mentioned as subject. It is common in news and writing.

examples.en: The meeting is proceeding smoothly.
They adjusted the signals so that traffic flows smoothly.

examples.ko: 소통이 원활히 되려면 서로 잘 들어야 해요.
examples.en: For communication to go smoothly, you must listen well to each other.
The internet isn't connecting smoothly.
Please help everyone finish the event without a hitch.
Stretch often so that your blood circulates well.

explain: 일상에서는 '순조롭게'나 '잘'이라고 하고, '원활히'는 조금 격식 있는 말이에요. 소통, 교통, 진행, 공급처럼 막힘없이 흐르는 일에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The work is going smoothly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '원활히'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때는 '원활하게'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 원활히; 원활하게 is more common in speech.

phrases.en: Communication on our team is smooth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사가 아닌 형용사 형태라서 문장 끝에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form, which can end a sentence.

phrases.en: The work finished smoothly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '원활히' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday word to use in place of 원활히.

explain_en: In daily talk people say '순조롭게' or '잘', and '원활히' is a bit more formal. It suits things that flow without blockage, such as communication, traffic, progress and supply.

examples.en: I became a committee member and received a letter of appointment.
The ceremony for presenting letters of appointment is held in the morning.
The term of office is written on the letter of appointment.
The letter of appointment was handed to the new advisory member.
Please keep your letter of appointment safe.
I received a letter of appointment together with a business card.

explain: 위원, 자문위원, 홍보대사처럼 어떤 역할을 맡아 달라고 할 때 주는 증서예요. 보통 '위촉장을 받다/수여하다/전달하다'로 쓰고, 공식 행사나 공공기관 소식에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The mayor presented letters of appointment to the committee members.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주는 쪽이 공식 행사에서 줄 때 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression for the giving side at an official ceremony.
phrases.en_equiv: to present a letter of appointment

phrases.en: A staff member delivered the letter of appointment in person.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수여하다'보다 덜 딱딱하고 건네주는 행동에 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less formal than '수여하다', focusing on the act of handing it over.
phrases.en_equiv: to deliver a letter of appointment

phrases.en: I kept the letter of appointment I received in a safe place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받은 뒤에 간직하는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for keeping it after you have received it.
phrases.en_equiv: to keep a letter of appointment

explain_en: It is the certificate given when someone is asked to take on a role such as committee member, adviser or ambassador. It is normally used as '위촉장을 받다/수여하다/전달하다' and often appears in official events and public-institution news.

en: to be resolved by vote (in a meeting or assembly)

examples.en: The new budget was approved at yesterday's meeting.
This item was passed by a majority vote.

examples.ko: 규칙이 의결되면 다음 달부터 바로 시행돼요.
examples.en: Once the rule is passed, it takes effect from next month.
We will post what was resolved on the website.

examples.ko: 회장 선출안이 만장일치로 의결될 것 같아요.
examples.en: It looks like the proposal to elect a chair will pass unanimously.

examples.ko: 안건이 의결되지 않아서 회의가 다음 주로 미뤄졌어요.
examples.en: The item wasn't passed, so the meeting was postponed to next week.

explain: 의결되다는 회의에서 투표나 합의로 안건이 정해질 때 써요. 개인이 정하는 일에는 쓰지 않고 '결정하다'를 써요. 비슷한 '가결되다'는 안건이 통과됐다는 결과를, '부결되다'는 거절됐다는 결과를 말해요.

phrases.en: The committee passed the new budget plan by vote.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의결되다'의 능동형으로, 회의가 안건을 정한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form of 의결되다, meaning a meeting decides a matter.

phrases.en: That item was resolved unanimously.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모두가 찬성해 정해졌다는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that says everyone agreed and it was decided.

phrases.en: The bill was passed in the National Assembly yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의결되다'가 정해지는 일이라면 '가결되다'는 통과됐다는 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: While 의결되다 is about being decided, 가결되다 stresses the result of passing.

explain_en: 의결되다 is used when a meeting settles an item by a vote or agreement. Do not use it for something one person decides; use 결정하다 there. Similar words: 가결되다 means the item passed and 부결되다 means it was rejected.

dis.h: formal; decided by a group vote

p.n: 결정 loses the sense of a formal vote by a committee.

examples.ko: 계획에 허점이 보여서 전체를 재검토해야 해요.
examples.en: I saw gaps in the plan, so we have to review all of it again.

examples.ko: 이 결정은 재검토할 여지가 있다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think there is room to reconsider this decision.

examples.ko: 내일까지 예산안을 한 번 더 재검토해 주세요.
examples.en: Please review the budget proposal once more by tomorrow.
The team leader told me to review the report again.
Before submitting, I carefully rechecked the numbers.

examples.ko: 문제가 계속 생겨서 계약 조건을 재검토하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Problems kept arising, so we decided to reconsider the contract terms.

explain: 이미 정한 일을 다시 따져 볼 때 써요. '다시 재검토하다'는 '재'와 '다시'가 겹쳐서 어색해요. '재검토 중이다', '재검토가 필요하다'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I'll check the content again and review it once more.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다시 살펴보겠다고 약속할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to promise that you will look at something again.

phrases.en: This plan needs to be reconsidered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사로 쓰면 다시 살펴볼 필요가 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a noun, it says something needs to be looked at again.

phrases.en: We're reconsidering the plan right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 다시 따져 보고 있는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you are in the middle of reviewing something again.

explain_en: Use it when taking another look at something already decided. '다시 재검토하다' sounds odd because '재' and '다시' both mean 'again'. It is also often used as a noun, as in '재검토 중이다' or '재검토가 필요하다'.

examples.en: The judge concluded the trial.

examples.ko: 회사는 이번 달에 조사를 종결할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will wrap up the investigation this month.
We decided to end the discussion here.
The CEO closed the meeting and stood up.
I want to put an end to the old argument.
To settle the matter, you both have to apologize.

explain: '끝내다'의 딱딱한 말이에요. 회의·재판·조사처럼 공식적인 일에 주로 써요. 사람이 일부러 끝내면 '종결하다', 저절로 끝나면 '종결되다'예요.

phrases.en: The police closed the investigation because there was no evidence.
phrases.nuance_ko: '종결하다'와 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말로, 조사나 수사를 공식적으로 끝낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing with 종결하다, used when officially ending an investigation.

phrases.en: The chairperson said the meeting is concluded for today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의를 공식적으로 마칠 때 쓰는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression for officially wrapping up a meeting.

phrases.en: That case was closed last week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 일부러 끝내면 '종결하다', 일이 끝난 상태를 말하면 '종결되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 종결하다 when someone ends it on purpose, and 종결되다 when describing that it has ended.

explain_en: The stiff version of '끝내다', used mostly for formal things like meetings, trials and investigations. A person ending it on purpose is '종결하다'; something ending by itself is '종결되다'.

dis.h: formal: concludes a case or war

p.n: 종료하다 is possible but plainer; 종결하다 stresses a final settlement.

examples.en: At a shareholders' meeting, agenda items are usually passed by majority vote.

examples.ko: 주총의 의결 사항은 홈페이지에서 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can check the resolutions of the shareholders' meeting on the website.

examples.ko: 이번 주총은 다음 달 말에 열려요.
examples.en: This shareholders' meeting will be held at the end of next month.

examples.ko: 주총에 참석하지 못하면 위임장을 보낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you can't attend the shareholders' meeting, you can send a proxy form.

examples.ko: 많은 회사가 비슷한 시기에 주총을 열어요.
examples.en: Many companies hold their shareholders' meetings around the same time.
The results of the shareholders' meeting were on the news.

explain: '주주총회'의 줄임말이에요. 뉴스나 경제 기사에서 많이 나오고, 회사의 주식을 가진 사람들이 모여 중요한 일을 결정하는 자리예요. 말할 때나 기사 제목에서는 줄여서 '주총'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The shareholders' meeting will be held next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주총'의 원래 말로, 서류나 공식적인 글에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of 주총, used in documents and formal writing.

phrases.en: The company will hold a shareholders' meeting next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주총을 시작하거나 여는 일을 말할 때 쓰는 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic collocation for holding a shareholders' meeting.

phrases.example: 정기 주총은 보통 일 년에 한 번 해요.
phrases.en: The regular shareholders' meeting is usually held once a year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해마다 정해진 때에 하는 주총을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the shareholders' meeting held at a set time every year.

explain_en: It is the short form of '주주총회'. It appears often in news and economic articles, and refers to the meeting where people who own shares of a company gather to decide important matters. In speech and headlines, it is shortened to '주총'.

examples.en: A new executive board was elected for the student council.
At the executive board meeting, we decided this year's plan.
The union's executive board decided to meet with the company boss.
The executive board members help prepare the event.
I want to join the club's executive board.

examples.ko: 집행부와 일반 회원들의 의견이 서로 달랐어요.
examples.en: The executive board and the regular members had different opinions.

explain: 집행부는 학생회, 노조, 동호회처럼 모임을 실제로 운영하는 사람들이에요. 안건을 정하는 '총회'와 달리 정한 일을 실행하는 쪽이라 이름에 '집행'이 들어가요. 나라의 정부 쪽은 '행정부'라고 불러서 구분해요.

phrases.en: I'm an executive board member of the club.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집행부에서 일하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a person who works on the executive board.

phrases.en: The new executive board started preparing for the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임이 새로 바뀐 운영진을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the newly changed management of a group.

phrases.en: The students chose the executive board by voting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운영할 사람들을 정할 때 '뽑다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 뽑다 when choosing the people to run something.

explain_en: 집행부 is the group that actually runs an organization such as a student council, union or club. Unlike a 총회 (general meeting) that decides agenda items, it carries out what was decided, hence 집행 in the name. In national government the equivalent is called 행정부.

examples.en: The parents observed the class.
I am going to the court tomorrow to observe a trial.
Teachers observe classes at other schools.

examples.ko: 공장 견학에서 작업 과정을 참관할 수 있어요.
examples.en: On the factory tour, you can observe the work process.
The person who observed the exam wrote a confirmation.
You have to stay quiet while you observe.

explain: '참관하다'는 직접 하지 않고 그 자리에 있으면서 지켜보는 거예요. '구경하다'는 재미로 보는 것이고, '참관하다'는 공식적인 자리나 일을 볼 때 써요. '수업 참관', '재판 참관'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 다음 주에 학부모 수업 참관이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a parent class observation next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사로 쓰여 수업을 지켜보는 공식적인 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a noun for an official event of observing a class.

phrases.example: 선거 때 참관인이 투표 과정을 지켜봤어요.
phrases.en: An observer watched the voting process during the election.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 하지 않고 공정하게 지켜보는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who watches impartially without taking part.

phrases.example: 저는 내일 공개 재판을 참관하러 가요.
phrases.en: I'm going to observe a public trial tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)러 가다'를 붙여 지켜보려고 간다는 목적을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -(으)러 가다, it states the purpose of going to observe.

explain_en: With '참관하다' you are present and watching without taking part. '구경하다' is looking for fun, while '참관하다' is for official events or work. It is also common as a noun: '수업 참관' (class observation), '재판 참관' (trial observation).

en: to be selected; to be chosen

examples.en: My idea was adopted at the meeting.
The adopted plan takes effect from next week.

examples.ko: 이 의견이 최종안으로 채택될 것 같아요.
examples.en: This opinion looks likely to be adopted as the final plan.
I was glad that my writing was picked for the newspaper.
Proposals that weren't adopted are also valuable opinions.
It's a message board where good answers are selected.

explain: 여러 가지 안 중에서 하나가 골라져 쓰이게 될 때 써요. '선택되다'보다 공식적이고, 의견, 방안, 제안에 많이 써요. 사람을 뽑는 경우는 '채용되다'와 구별하세요.

phrases.en: My opinion was adopted at the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의견, 방안, 제안과 가장 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs best with opinions, plans, and proposals.
phrases.en_equiv: for an opinion to be adopted

phrases.en: Unfortunately, my proposal wasn't chosen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뽑히지 못했을 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form used when something was not chosen.

phrases.en: This method was chosen in the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 일상적인 말이에요. '채택되다'는 공식적인 자리에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday; 채택되다 fits formal settings.

explain_en: Used when one among several options is picked for use. More official than '선택되다', and common for opinions, plans and proposals. Don't confuse it with '채용되다', which is for hiring people.

p.n: 선정되다 does not fit an opinion; 채택되다 means it was adopted.

examples.ko: 주민 총회가 이번 주 토요일에 열려요.
examples.en: The residents' general meeting is this Saturday.
We elected a new president at the general meeting.
I took a day off to attend the general meeting.
The club holds a general meeting at year-end.
Please read the general meeting materials in advance.
The general meeting ended in an hour.

explain: '정기 총회', '임시 총회'처럼 앞에 말이 붙는 일이 많아요. 회사에서는 '주주총회'라고 해요. 아파트나 동호회에서도 총회를 열어요.

phrases.example: 우리 동호회는 일 년에 한 번 정기 총회를 열어요.
phrases.en: Our club holds a regular general meeting once a year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해마다 또는 정해진 때에 여는 총회를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A general meeting held on a set schedule, such as every year.

phrases.en: A problem came up, so they held a special general meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 필요해서 따로 여는 총회를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A general meeting called separately because of an urgent need.

phrases.en: I will attend this general meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 총회에 가서 함께한다고 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for saying you will go to and take part in the meeting.

explain_en: A modifier often comes before it, as in 정기 총회 or 임시 총회. In companies it is 주주총회. Apartment complexes and clubs also hold a 총회.

en: to meet; to gather; to assemble

examples.en: The two leaders will meet in Seoul tomorrow.
The representatives decided to meet at lunch.
The lawmakers met behind closed doors yesterday.
I hope the ruling and opposition leaders can meet again after a long time.
The ministers met and discussed countermeasures.
I heard they plan to meet on the weekend.

explain: 뉴스에서 중요한 인물들이 모여 의논할 때 써요. 가까운 사람끼리는 '만나다', '모이다'가 자연스러워요. '~와/과 회동하다'처럼 함께 만나는 상대를 '와/과'로 말해요.

phrases.en: The president met with the prime minister.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 만나는 상대를 '와/과'로 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person met with is marked with 와/과.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 회동한 뒤에 기자회견을 열었어요.
phrases.en: After meeting, the two held a press conference.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만남 다음에 일어난 일을 이어서 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form for what happened after the meeting.

phrases.example: 양국 대표가 다음 주에 회동할 예정이에요.
phrases.en: The two countries' representatives are scheduled to meet next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 있을 만남을 알리는 뉴스 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style way to announce an upcoming meeting.

explain_en: It is used in the news when important people gather to discuss something. Between close people '만나다' or '모이다' sounds natural. The other party is marked with '와/과', as in '~와/과 회동하다'.

p.n: 만나다 is plain; 회동하다 is news-style for important people meeting for talks.
